# Requirements

Generated from `docs/SRS-RI-v0.1.md` at commit 9a3e8b6 2026-11-11. 180 requirements
in 28 groups, every one at status *Draft* until the SRS is approved
(the SRS header says so). The *release* column is the first release named; where

Each component is one tracker table; the [progress](progress.html) page counts a *Draft*

## 3.2.1 CLI

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-CLI-001 | The CLI SHALL expose `build`, `inspect`, `run`, `bench`, `serve` and `tune`, SHALL exit non-zero on failure, and SHALL print one structured error line (`error=<code> component=<name> detail=<text>`) to stderr on failure. *Rationale: One entry point; failures scriptable.* | Critical | Draft | R1 (build, inspect, run, tune); R2 (bench); R3 (serve) |
| RI-CLI-002 | `build --model <dir> --target <arch> --out <file> [--precision] [--profile] [--kv-dtype] [--tp N] [--ep N] [--lora-max-rank R]` SHALL produce an artifact or fail without leaving a file at `<out>`. *Rationale: UC-01; RI-ART-004.* | Critical | Draft | R1 (core); R2 (--kv-dtype, --tp); R3 (--ep, --lora-max-rank) |
| RI-CLI-003 | `run` and `serve` SHALL accept an artifact or a model directory; given a model directory they SHALL build an artifact into `RUSTINFER_CACHE_DIR` (default `~/.cache/rustinfer`) keyed by model hash, target, precision and profile, and SHALL reuse it on later loads. *Rationale: ADR-006; every incumbent engine builds on first load with a cache.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CLI-004 | `--require-prebuilt`, and the server key `strict_artifact`, SHALL make `run` and `serve` refuse a model directory and refuse to build. *Rationale: A production start never compiles.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CLI-005 | `inspect <file>` SHALL print header, target, producer, LLVM version, profile, precision per weight class, KV geometry, catalog entries with resource reports, arena and weight sizes, input hashes, build options and whether the artifact came from `build` or a first load, without initialising a device. *Rationale: UC-02.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CLI-006 | `run <artifact or dir> --prompt-tokens <ids>  or  --prompt <text>` SHALL load the artifact, refuse a target mismatch, and print generated tokens; sampling flags SHALL map one-to-one to RI-SMP. *Rationale: UC-03.* | High | Draft | R1 (token ids); R2 (text through the tokenizer) |
| RI-CLI-007 | `tune --target <arch> [--generator <name>] [--shapes <file>]` SHALL run the autotuner on the current device and write catalog entries. *Rationale: RI-KC-006.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CLI-008 | `bench throughput or latency --engine <file> --dataset <file or synthetic:...> --concurrency N [--streaming]` SHALL report TTFT, TPOT, ITL at p50, p90 and p99, output tokens per second and requests per second, in text and JSON. *Rationale: UC-12.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-CLI-009 | `serve <artifact or dir> [--host] [--port] [--config <yaml>] [--set k=v]` SHALL start the server of RI-SRV with YAML configuration overridden by `--set`. *Rationale: UC-18.* | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-CLI-010 | Every subcommand SHALL log a version manifest once at start: crate version, rustc version, LLVM version, host triple and each direct dependency version. *Rationale: SWG-001 §8.4.5.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CLI-011 | Every log line SHALL be `key=value` text with an ISO-8601 timestamp, level and component, on stderr; the level SHALL come from `RUSTINFER_LOG` (default `info`); stdout SHALL carry only results. *Rationale: SWG-001 §8.4.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CLI-012 | Every path argument SHALL be canonicalised and checked (inputs exist, outputs have a writable parent) before any work starts. *Rationale: SWG-001 §8.7.* | High | Draft | R1 |

## 3.2.2 Frontend

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-FE-001 | The frontend SHALL lower the LLaMA family (`llama`, `mistral`, `qwen2`, `qwen3`) from `config.json` into Model IR: layers, hidden size, attention and KV heads, intermediate size, vocabulary, RoPE parameters and scaling, norm epsilon, tied embeddings. *Rationale: UC-01.* | Critical | Draft | R1 (llama); R2 (the rest) |
| RI-FE-002 | The frontend SHALL map every HF parameter to the Model IR weight it feeds and SHALL fail naming the first missing or unexpected parameter. *Rationale: A silent weight mismatch is wrong output, not an error.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-FE-003 | An unsupported `model_type` SHALL be rejected with an error naming it and the supported list. *Rationale: UC-21.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-FE-004 | The frontend SHALL read only `config.json` and the safetensors shard headers at build and SHALL emit the weight manifest (RI-ART-005); weight bytes are read by Sluice at load (RI-WST). *Rationale: Trillion-parameter checkpoints; build time and host memory independent of* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-FE-005 | The frontend SHALL lower MoE families (DeepSeek-V3 with MLA, Qwen MoE, GPT-OSS): router, experts, shared experts, MLA latent projections. *Rationale: UC-14.* | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-FE-006 | Pre-quantized checkpoints (FP8 per-tensor and block-scale; AWQ, GPTQ, MXFP4) SHALL be imported with their scales and SHALL be rejected when the target has no catalog kernel for the scheme. *Rationale: INV §1.* | High | Draft | R2 (FP8); R3 (AWQ, GPTQ, MXFP4) |
| RI-FE-007 | A LoRA adapter directory SHALL be read into adapter weights keyed by target module, with rank checked against the artifact's `max_lora_rank`. *Rationale: UC-15.* | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-FE-008 | A model given as a Model IR JSON document SHALL be accepted in place of an HF directory. *Rationale: Custom architectures; the Model IR is the contract.* | Low | Draft | R2 |

## 3.2.3 Model IR

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-MIR-001 | The Model IR SHALL be a typed SSA graph: each node applies one operator to named input tensors and defines named outputs; the graph SHALL be acyclic. *Rationale: One contract for every frontend and backend (ADR-005).* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-MIR-002 | A shape SHALL be a list of dimensions, each a static integer or a named dynamic dimension from the set `batch`, `num_tokens`, `seq_len`, `beam`, bounded by the profile. *Rationale: Semi-static artifact (INV §0).* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-MIR-003 | Dtypes SHALL be bf16, fp16, fp32, fp8 (OCP e4m3, FNUZ e4m3), int8, int4x2, fp4x2, e8m0, int32, int64, bool, each with a defined element size; quantized tensors SHALL carry a descriptor (scheme, group size, scale dtype). *Rationale: The formats AMD matrix cores take.* | High | Draft | R1 (bf16, fp16, fp32, fp8, int32, int64, bool); R2 (int8, fp4x2, e8m0); R3 (int4x2) |
| RI-MIR-004 | The operator set SHALL be: embedding, matmul (bias, scales), rmsnorm, layernorm, rope, attention_prefill, attention_decode_paged, kv_cache_write, silu_and_mul, gelu_and_mul, residual_add, quantize, dequantize, logits_head, sample, moe_route, moe_experts, lora_apply, collective, and fused (the composition of its parts). *Rationale: Sufficient for the supported families; fusion needs a fused node.* | Critical | Draft | R1 (LLaMA subset); R2 (collective); R3 (moe_*, lora_apply) |
| RI-MIR-005 | Every tensor SHALL carry a placement slot (memory tier) and every node a device slot, empty after the frontend and filled by the planner. *Rationale: RI-PLN-003.* | High | Draft | R1 (slots); R2 (filled) |
| RI-MIR-006 | Validation SHALL reject a cycle, an undefined input, a tensor defined twice, a dtype mismatch at an input, or a dynamic dimension outside the set, naming the node. *Rationale: Malformed graphs stop before the compiler.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-MIR-007 | The Model IR SHALL round-trip through a canonical JSON form (sorted keys, exact numerics) without loss, and the artifact SHALL carry it. *Rationale: Inspection, golden tests, RI-FE-008, Apple's portable-IR property.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-MIR-008 | The Model IR SHALL be versioned independently of the artifact format, with a reader that accepts a listed set of versions. *Rationale: SWG-001 §14.4.* | Medium | Draft | R1 |

## 3.2.4 Graph compiler

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-GC-001 | The graph compiler SHALL run an ordered pass pipeline and SHALL log each pass's name, node count before and after, and duration at `info`. *Rationale: An attributable pipeline.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-002 | Shape inference SHALL resolve every tensor under the profile and SHALL fail on an unresolved dimension, a profile violating min ≤ opt ≤ max, or a `max_num_tokens` not a multiple of the KV block size. *Rationale: INV §2.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-003 | Fusion SHALL replace matched sequences (rmsnorm→matmul, matmul→silu_and_mul, residual_add→rmsnorm, rope→kv_cache_write, quantize→matmul, elementwise chains) with fused nodes only when the catalog lists a kernel or the fuser (RI-KC-010) can produce one. *Rationale: Target-dependent fusion.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-004 | The precision pass SHALL assign each matmul and attention a weight and activation format from the build options or the imported quantization, and SHALL insert the quantize and scale nodes the chosen kernel requires. *Rationale: Quantization is a build decision.* | High | Draft | R1 (bf16, fp8); R2 (int8, MXFP4, fp8 KV); R3 (int4 weight-only) |
| RI-GC-005 | Kernel selection SHALL choose one catalog kernel per node by (operator, dtypes, layout, shape rules at `opt`) ordered by tuned cost, record the kernel id in the Plan, request a missing bucket from the kernel compiler when a device is present (RI-KC-006), and otherwise fail naming the node. *Rationale: No run-time selection; no fallback.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-006 | Memory planning SHALL assign every intermediate an offset in one activation arena sized at the profile's `max`, reusing non-overlapping lifetimes, and SHALL record the arena size, KV block geometry and per-sequence state sizes. *Rationale: Allocate once.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-007 | The Plan SHALL be an ordered list of launches with kernel id, argument bindings (arena offset, weight id, KV pool, request-state field, scalar), shape expressions over the dynamic dimensions, and sub-plans for prefill, decode and a mixed iteration. *Rationale: The runtime executes it verbatim.* | Critical | Draft | R1 (prefill, decode); R2 (mixed) |
| RI-GC-008 | The layout pass SHALL record, per weight, the layout the selected kernel declares and the transform from the source layout, as entries of the weight manifest and as load-phase launches of the Plan; the transform SHALL run at load on the device (RI-RT-001), never at build and never to disk. *Rationale: Matrix-core tiled weights; a wrong layout is silent corruption; the* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-009 | Compilation SHALL be deterministic: identical inputs and options SHALL give byte-identical Plan, catalog and kernel sections. *Rationale: Reproducible artifacts.* | Medium | Draft | R1 |
| RI-GC-010 | `--tp N` SHALL shard attention heads and MLP columns across N ranks, insert collective nodes and emit one Plan per rank. *Rationale: UC-13.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-GC-011 | `--ep N` SHALL place experts across N ranks (EP-only or hybrid with TP), insert dispatch and combine nodes and record expert placement. *Rationale: UC-14.* | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-GC-012 | LoRA application points SHALL be reserved on every matmul marked adaptable, with `max_lora_rank` fixed in the Plan. *Rationale: UC-15.* | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-GC-013 | A verification sub-plan for speculative decoding SHALL be emitted when requested, bounded by `max_draft_tokens`. *Rationale: UC-16.* | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-GC-014 | A build whose feature combination is not marked supported in `docs/feature-matrix.md` SHALL be refused naming the pair. *Rationale: RI-SEC-005.* | High | Draft | R1 |

## 3.2.5 Kernel compiler

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-KC-001 | Kernels SHALL be written as Rust generators: functions taking a parameter struct (dtypes, tiles, layouts, pipeline depth, fused epilogue) and emitting Kernel IR through a builder; no kernel SHALL exist as MLIR text, HIP, OpenCL or assembly source except through a generator (RI-KC-009). *Rationale: ADR-005; the generator is the unit the autotuner explores.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-002 | The Kernel IR SHALL be an MLIR dialect at tile level with explicit layouts: tiles, memory spaces (global, shared, register), barriers, a matrix-multiply op, masked loads and stores, reductions, structured control flow; thread identity SHALL NOT appear. *Rationale: A tile IR retargets to SIMT, vector and mesh devices; a thread IR does not.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-003 | AMD lowering SHALL go through the MLIR `gpu` pipeline to `rocdl` and the LLVM AMDGPU back end, emitting MFMA for the matrix op with each architecture's formats (bf16; fp8 FNUZ on gfx942; OCP fp8, fp4, fp6 with e8m0 on gfx950), LDS for shared tiles, and bounds-checked buffer loads. *Rationale: The first target.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-004 | RISC-V lowering SHALL be rustinfer's own: Kernel IR to a vector form (RVV with the matrix extensions where the core has them) through the LLVM RISC-V back end, and to a mesh form for Tensix-class devices through their open MLIR dialect; the SPIR-V path for Vulkan-class devices SHALL use MLIR's `spirv` dialect. *Rationale: No vendor kernel exists on RISC-V; the IR must be ours end to end.* | High | Draft | R2 (spirv, compile-tested); R3 (riscv-vector, compile-tested); R4 (riscv-mesh) |
| RI-KC-005 | The R1 generator set SHALL cover GEMM (bf16, fp8; bias, scale and activation epilogues), attention prefill, paged attention decode, rmsnorm, rope with cache write, silu_and_mul, embedding, residual add, quantize, logits head and sampling; R3 adds MoE routing and expert GEMMs, MLA attention, LoRA application and speculative verification. *Rationale: The catalog of a transformer, as MLX keeps one.* | Critical | Draft | R1; R3 as listed |
| RI-KC-006 | The autotuner SHALL run a generator over its declared parameter space on the device, check each variant against the CPU reference, keep the fastest correct variant per shape bucket, and write the catalog entry (parameters, cost, binary hash, resource report); catalogs SHALL be committed per target and merged with no duplicate keys. *Rationale: The tuned table is ours now.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-007 | No kernel SHALL enter the catalog or an artifact without validation against the CPU reference at its catalogued shapes within a per-dtype tolerance. *Rationale: Correctness before speed.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-008 | Compilation to a binary SHALL use no external process: LLVM and `lld` as libraries, the target's module loader for the result. *Rationale: No toolchain dependency at build or load.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-009 | A generator MAY emit target assembly instead of Kernel IR for one hot kernel on one architecture; it SHALL register through the same catalog interface and pass RI-KC-007. *Rationale: The last fraction of performance, when measured to be needed (OI-001).* | Medium | Draft | R4 |
| RI-KC-010 | One fusion generator SHALL compose chains of elementwise and reduction ops into a single kernel; no general-purpose fusion compiler SHALL be written. *Rationale: MLX's split: a fixed catalog plus a small fuser.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-KC-011 | Kernel compilation SHALL be deterministic for the same generator, parameters, target and LLVM version; the artifact SHALL record the LLVM version. *Rationale: Reproducibility.* | Medium | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KC-012 | Every catalog entry SHALL carry a resource report (registers, LDS, occupancy) and `inspect` SHALL print it. *Rationale: Tuning without a profiler in hand.* | Medium | Draft | R2 |
| RI-KC-013 | A catalog entry SHALL record the hardware it was validated on (architecture, driver version, date); an entry SHALL NOT be used on an architecture it was not validated on. *Rationale: gfx950 and the CDNA successor share nothing but a CU count.* | High | Draft | R1 |

## 3.2.6 Topology planner

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-PLN-001 | The topology model SHALL describe devices (architecture, compute kind, matrix formats, phase affinity, local tier, graph capture), memory tiers (capacity, read and write bandwidth, latency, sharing scope, reachable set with mechanism), links (endpoints, bandwidth, latency, adjacency, hardware collectives) and offload engines (functions they can own), serialisable to and from JSON. *Rationale: DEV §9; the interfaces exist from the first release.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-PLN-002 | Discovery SHALL populate the model from the node: HIP devices and peer access, PCIe and NUMA topology, DRAM, CXL devices, NVMe devices, RDMA-capable NICs, DPUs; what cannot be probed SHALL be absent, never guessed. *Rationale: Nodes differ; the planner must see the real one.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-PLN-003 | The planner SHALL fill the Model IR placement slots: weight residency per tensor, KV tier policy per layer, prefill and decode device sets, serving-stack function placement, expert placement, collective-to-link mapping, transfer path per cross-device edge, from a cost model over the topology, and SHALL explain each decision in the placement section. *Rationale: UC-19, DEV §9.* | High | Draft | R2 (GPU, host CPU, DRAM, NVMe, RDMA); R3 (CXL, expert placement); R4 (DPU functions) |
| RI-PLN-004 | Placement SHALL be computed at load from the discovered topology, cached beside the artifact keyed by topology hash, and pinnable; a pinned placement SHALL be refused on a differing topology. *Rationale: The artifact must not bake one node's topology in.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-PLN-005 | The artifact SHALL reserve `topology` and `placement` sections, empty at build unless pinned. *Rationale: Format stability.* | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-PLN-006 | The planner SHALL be able to place ingress, tokenization, streaming and KV eviction onto a DPU with general-purpose cores, running a rustinfer agent built for that ISA, with tokens delivered to device memory by RDMA. *Rationale: The CPU-free serving pattern on Pensando Salina or a merchant DPU.* | Medium | Draft | R4 |

## 3.2.7 Artifact

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-ART-001 | The artifact SHALL begin with the fixed header of ADR-002: magic, format version, header length, target, producer, SHA-256 of all following bytes, section count, section table. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-002 | Sections SHALL be `model_ir`, `plan`, `profile`, `metadata`, `catalog`, `kernels`, `weights` (the weight manifest, RI-ART-012), `topology`, `placement`, and from R3 `lora_slots`, each with its own offset, length and alignment, addressable independently. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-003 | The reader SHALL refuse an artifact whose magic, version, header length, section bounds or hash fail, naming the failed check. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-004 | The writer SHALL stream to a temporary file in the destination directory, write the hash last, `fsync`, and rename; an interrupted build SHALL leave no file at the destination. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-005 | The weight manifest SHALL record, per weight id, the source file, tensor name, dtype, shape, source layout and byte range, the target layout and transform (RI-GC-008), and the ranks that need it; the loader SHALL read source bytes by that range so no tensor is read by a rank that does not need it. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-006 | The reader SHALL list the format versions it accepts; a bump SHALL be recorded in `docs/api/CHANGELOG.md` with a migration note. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-007 | A multi-rank build SHALL produce one artifact per rank carrying `rank`, `world_size` and the parallel layout; ranks from different builds SHALL be refused together. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-ART-008 | `metadata` SHALL record build options, producer, rustc and LLVM versions, catalog version, the checkpoint identity (hash of `config.json`, of every safetensors header and of the file sizes; never of the weight bytes), origin (`build` or first load) and timestamp. | Medium | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-009 | An artifact SHALL serve every batch size, token count and sequence length inside its `profile` section without a rebuild; only a new model, target, precision or profile range SHALL invalidate it (RI-MIR-002, ADR-006). | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-010 | Autotuning results SHALL live in the catalog, keyed by target, generator version and shape bucket, independent of any artifact; a build SHALL copy the entries it uses into `catalog` and SHALL NOT re-tune a kernel the catalog already holds for that key, so a model or compiler change reuses every entry whose key still matches. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ART-011 | Each release SHALL publish prebuilt artifacts for the reference models on every supported target of `docs/hardware.md`, so `--require-prebuilt` is the normal production path and build on first load is the fallback for a target without a published artifact. | Medium | Draft | R2 |
| RI-ART-012 | An artifact SHALL NOT contain weight bytes. It SHALL reference the checkpoint through the weight manifest, `run` and `serve` SHALL locate the checkpoint from the artifact's directory or `--weights <dir>`, SHALL refuse a checkpoint whose identity (RI-ART-008) differs from the manifest's, and SHALL offer `--verify-weights` for a full per-tensor hash check. *Rationale: A 2.4T-parameter checkpoint is near 5 TB; copying it into an engine file is* | Critical | Draft | R1 |

## 3.2.8 Target abstraction

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-TGT-001 | A target SHALL be identified by an architecture string and resolved from it only; product names SHALL NOT be interpreted. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-TGT-002 | The `Target` trait SHALL be composed of `Catalog` (device-free), `Device` (enumeration, properties, buffers, streams, events, copies, graphs) and `Launcher` (execute a Plan entry), as in ADR-003. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-TGT-003 | The CPU reference target SHALL implement every R1 operator in Rust with fp32 accumulation and the collectives as in-process loops; it is the correctness oracle for every other target. | Critical | Draft | R1 (operators); R2 (collectives) |
| RI-TGT-004 | Adding a target SHALL require a new crate, one architecture registry entry and one Kernel IR lowering; nothing in the graph compiler, planner or runtime. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-TGT-005 | `Device` SHALL support capturing a sub-plan into a device graph and replaying it, with eager launches as the fallback. | High | Draft | R2 |

## 3.2.9 ROCm backend

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-ROC-001 | The ROCm target SHALL bind `libamdhip64` for devices, memory, streams, events, module loading, launches and graph capture through one FFI module. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ROC-002 | Every HIP error SHALL become a typed error carrying the HIP error string and the failed operation. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ROC-003 | The architecture SHALL be read from `gcnArchName`; an artifact for another architecture SHALL be refused. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ROC-004 | Code objects SHALL be loaded with the HIP module loader after the artifact check, and each kernel's LDS and register needs SHALL be checked against the device before its first launch. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ROC-005 | `unsafe` SHALL be confined to `rustinfer-target-rocm::ffi` with a `SAFETY` comment per block. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-ROC-006 | Collectives SHALL go through RCCL, and for messages below a configurable size through rustinfer's own IPC all-reduce kernel. | High | Draft | R2 (RCCL); R3 (own all-reduce) |
| RI-ROC-007 | The decode sub-plan SHALL be captured into a HIP graph per batch-size bucket and replayed. | High | Draft | R2 |

## 3.2.10 RISC-V backends

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-RV-001 | The workspace SHALL contain target crates `riscv-vector`, `riscv-mesh` and `spirv-vulkan`, each implementing `Target`, registered under their architecture strings, compiling on every host. | Medium | Draft | R1 (stubs); R2 (spirv-vulkan lowering); R3 (riscv-vector lowering); R4 (riscv-mesh) |
| RI-RV-002 | A build for a stub target SHALL fail at kernel selection with "catalog empty", proving the abstraction end to end. | Medium | Draft | R1 |
| RI-RV-003 | A RISC-V backend SHALL be brought up on hardware in this order: lowering compile-tested, CPU-reference parity for every R1 generator, autotuned catalog committed with validation records, op tests; no catalog entry without hardware validation (RI-KC-013). | Medium | Draft | R3 (first device) |
| RI-RV-004 | The `riscv-vector` lowering SHALL target RVV 1.0 with a vector-length-agnostic tile mapping and SHALL use a core's matrix extension when the catalog entry records it. | Medium | Draft | R3 |

## 3.2.11 Executor

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-RT-001 | The executor SHALL load an artifact, verify the target and the checkpoint identity, run the planner, allocate the arena, KV pool and per-sequence state once, then have Sluice stream every weight the rank needs into device memory in its target layout (RI-WST), before the first request; no device allocation SHALL occur on the request path. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-RT-002 | Each iteration SHALL execute the Plan's launches in order with no kernel selection, shape inference or allocation. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-RT-003 | The API SHALL provide `enqueue(Request) -> RequestId`, `await_responses (timeout)`, `cancel(RequestId)`, `iteration_stats()`, `request_stats()`, callable from several threads. | Critical | Draft | R1 (enqueue, await); R2 (cancel, stats, streaming) |
| RI-RT-004 | A `Request` SHALL carry prompt tokens, `SamplingConfig`, `OutputConfig` (logprobs, logits, streaming), `max_new_tokens`, optional stop and bad words, optional LoRA id, optional guided-decoding spec, optional priority and deadline. | Critical | Draft | R1 (core); R2 (output config, stop, bad words); R3 (lora, guided, priority, deadline) |
| RI-RT-005 | Streaming responses SHALL carry new tokens, finish reason and, when requested, logprobs, per iteration. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-RT-006 | A launch failure SHALL abort the affected batch with an error naming the Plan entry and kernel id, mark the requests failed, free their KV blocks, and leave the executor serving the next iteration. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-RT-007 | Cancellation SHALL take effect at the next iteration boundary and free KV blocks within it. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-RT-008 | One iteration SHALL run per device stream; an activation arena SHALL NOT be shared between concurrent iterations. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-RT-009 | A multi-rank artifact SHALL run with one process per rank, synchronised per iteration over the target's collectives. | High | Draft | R2 |

## 3.2.12 Scheduler

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-SCH-001 | New requests SHALL be admitted between iterations into one padding-free iteration with prefill requests first (in-flight batching). | Critical | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SCH-002 | Decode tokens SHALL be scheduled before prefill tokens within `max_batch_size` and `max_num_tokens`. | Critical | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SCH-003 | Policies `max_utilization`, `guaranteed_no_evict` and `static_batch` SHALL be selectable; the default from R2 SHALL be `max_utilization` with chunked prefill on. *Rationale: The first-class workload.* | High | Draft | R1 (static_batch); R2 (the rest) |
| RI-SCH-004 | Chunked prefill SHALL split a prompt into KV-block-aligned chunks interleaved with decode under `max_num_tokens`. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SCH-005 | The overlap scheduler SHALL run the host work of iteration n during the device work of iteration n+1, on by default, disable-able per executor. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SCH-006 | Under `max_utilization`, when KV blocks run out the lowest-priority, most-recently-admitted decode request SHALL be paused and later resumed from its retained or recomputed prefix. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SCH-007 | Requests SHALL carry a priority (default 0) and optional deadline; admission SHALL order by priority then arrival; an expired request SHALL fail. | Medium | Draft | R3 |
| RI-SCH-008 | LoRA requests SHALL batch with base requests up to `max_loras` adapters per iteration. | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-SCH-009 | Iteration statistics SHALL record prefill and decode counts, scheduled tokens, KV blocks used and free, reuse hits, iteration latency and paused requests. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SCH-010 | The scheduler state SHALL be a single uniform token-level model for prefill, chunked prefill, decode, reuse and speculation (no separate queues per phase). *Rationale: vLLM V1's lesson: features compose when the scheduler is uniform.* | High | Draft | R2 |

## 3.2.13 KV cache

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-KVC-001 | The cache SHALL be a pool of fixed-size token blocks (power of two, default 32, recorded in the Plan) with a block table per sequence. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KVC-002 | Allocation and release SHALL be O(1) from one pre-allocated pool with an LRU free list; no per-block heap allocation at run time. *Rationale: vLLM V1's block pool; prefix reuse must cost nothing at a 0 percent hit rate.* | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KVC-003 | Pool size SHALL be the smaller of `free_gpu_memory_fraction` (default 0.9) and an explicit `max_tokens`, computed after weights and arena. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-KVC-004 | A sequence longer than the profile's `max_seq_len` SHALL be refused at admission. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-KVC-005 | Filled blocks SHALL be indexed in a radix tree by token prefix; a new request SHALL reuse matching blocks and skip their computation; reuse SHALL be on by default; hits and misses SHALL be counted. *Rationale: SGLang's RadixAttention; agent traffic served well by default.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-KVC-006 | Eviction SHALL be prioritised LRU with per-block priority (0 to 100, default 35) and optional retention windows; only unreferenced leaf blocks are evictable. | Medium | Draft | R3 |
| RI-KVC-007 | Evicted blocks MAY be offloaded to host DRAM, CXL memory or NVMe tiers under the planner's KV policy and restored on reuse. | Medium | Draft | R3 (DRAM, NVMe); R4 (CXL, remote) |
| RI-KVC-008 | FP8 and INT8 cache storage with per-block scales SHALL be supported where the catalog's attention kernels read them. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-KVC-009 | Per-layer attention windows SHALL be supported with a circular block buffer; beam search SHALL be refused with sliding windows. | Medium | Draft | R2 |

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-SMP-001 | Greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, top-p decay and seeded sampling SHALL run per request on device for the whole batch in one launch. | Critical | Draft | R1 (greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p); R2 (min-p, decay, seeds) |
| RI-SMP-002 | Repetition, presence and frequency penalties, `no_repeat_ngram_size`, embedding bias, min and max tokens, stop words and bad words SHALL be applied per request. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SMP-003 | Logprobs and top-k logprobs SHALL be returned from the same logits the sample was drawn from. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SMP-004 | A caller-supplied logits post-processor SHALL run per request on host between logits and sampling. | Medium | Draft | R2 |
| RI-SMP-005 | Beam search SHALL support `best_of`, `n`, length penalty, diversity rate and early stopping, bounded by `max_beam_width`. | Medium | Draft | R3 |
| RI-SMP-006 | Guided decoding SHALL accept a JSON schema, regex or grammar, compile it, and apply token masks on device each step; an uncompilable spec SHALL be refused at admission. | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-SMP-007 | Sampling SHALL be reproducible for the same seed, request, artifact and target. | Medium | Draft | R2 |

## 3.2.20 Security

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-SEC-001 | Path inputs SHALL be canonicalised; the only shared objects loaded SHALL be the HIP runtime and RCCL from the system library path; an artifact SHALL never name a symbol or path to load, and its code objects SHALL be loaded only after RI-ART-003 and RI-ROC-004 pass. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-SEC-002 | The artifact reader SHALL bound every length by the file size and reject overlapping or out-of-file sections before reading them. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-SEC-003 | `config.json`, safetensors headers, adapter configs and HTTP bodies SHALL be parsed with size limits into typed structures; unknown required fields SHALL be errors. | High | Draft | R1 (files); R3 (HTTP) |
| RI-SEC-004 | The build SHALL record SHA-256 hashes of every input file in `metadata`. | Medium | Draft | R1 |
| RI-SEC-005 | A feature combination not marked supported in `docs/feature-matrix.md` SHALL be refused at build or at admission, never attempted. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-SEC-006 | Grammar compilation and logits post-processors SHALL run under a per-request time budget; exceeding it fails the request, not the executor. | Medium | Draft | R3 |

## 3.2.21 Concurrency

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-CON-001 | The graph compiler SHALL be single-threaded per build in R1; a parallel pass SHALL first pass a concurrency review and update the concurrency diagram. | Low | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CON-002 | The executor SHALL own one device context per rank; submissions from many threads SHALL pass through one queue; device buffers SHALL be touched only by the executor thread. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-CON-003 | The overlap scheduler SHALL hand results between the device thread and the host thread through a bounded channel ordered per request id; a failure on either side SHALL leave the KV cache consistent. | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-CON-004 | The server SHALL run an async frontend that never blocks on the executor, with bounded queues and 429/503 backpressure. | High | Draft | R3 |
| RI-CON-005 | The autotuner SHALL run variants sequentially on one device and MAY distribute generators across devices by process. | Low | Draft | R1 |

## 3.2.22 Sluice, the weight streamer

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-WST-001 | Sluice SHALL take the weight manifest, a checkpoint root and a rank, and SHALL produce every weight that rank needs as a device buffer in the manifest's target layout, reading each source tensor by its byte range and nothing else. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-WST-002 | Host memory SHALL be bounded by a configurable staging budget (default `RUSTINFER_STAGING_BYTES`, 1 GiB) regardless of model size; a tensor larger than the budget SHALL be streamed in slices. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-WST-003 | Layout transforms SHALL run on the device as the load-phase launches recorded by the graph compiler (RI-GC-008); the staging buffer SHALL hold source layout only. The CPU reference target SHALL run the same transforms on the host. | Critical | Draft | R1 |
| RI-WST-004 | Shard reads, host-to-device copies and transforms SHALL overlap on separate queues so load throughput is bounded by the slowest of storage, interconnect and transform, not their sum; `iteration_stats()` SHALL expose load time, bytes and throughput per stage. | High | Draft | R1 (overlap); R2 (stats) |
| RI-WST-005 | Sluice SHALL verify dtype, shape and byte range of every tensor against the shard header before reading it and SHALL refuse the first mismatch naming the tensor; with `--verify-weights` it SHALL also check the per-tensor hash recorded in the manifest. | High | Draft | R1 |

## 3.3.1 Performance

| id | text | priority | status | release |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RI-NFR-001 | The decode path SHALL perform zero heap allocations after warm-up, verified by an allocation-counting test on the CPU target. | High | Draft | R1 |
| RI-NFR-002 | `inspect` SHALL complete in under 1 s for any artifact. | Medium | Draft | R1 |
| RI-NFR-003 | On gfx950 with Llama-3-8B in FP8 at batch 64 and 1k/1k input/output, rustinfer SHALL reach at least 70 percent of the output-token throughput of vLLM with the AITER backend on the same GPU and ROCm in R2, and at least 100 percent in R3, measured with `bench`. *Rationale: Industry standard means matching the incumbent on its own kernels, with ours.* | High | Draft | R2 (70%); R3 (100%) |
| RI-NFR-004 | Host overhead per iteration SHALL be under 500 µs at batch 64 on the reference host with the overlap scheduler disabled. *Rationale: vLLM V1 and SGLang showed host overhead is the bottleneck as GPUs get faster.* | High | Draft | R2 |
| RI-NFR-005 | Loading a 16 GB weight section SHALL take under 10 s from page cache. | Medium | Draft | R2 |
| RI-NFR-006 | A generated GEMM kernel SHALL reach at least 80 percent of the best AITER kernel for the same shape and dtype on gfx950 by the end of R2, measured per catalog bucket. *Rationale: OI-001; the kernel-level target behind RI-NFR-003.* | High | Draft | R2 |
